_about: A minimal MK configuration for answering file requests with mkfreq on a system that does not run the MK BBS (for example a binkd node). Put it in a directory as bbsconfig.json and point MKJSON at that directory. Keys that start with an underscore are notes and are ignored.
_binkd_cfg: In binkd.cfg, run the wrapper below for every file request that arrives (*S is the SRIF file binkd writes):   exec "/usr/local/bin/mkfreq-binkd *S" *.req
_wrapper: Save as /usr/local/bin/mkfreq-binkd and make it executable (chmod 755). binkd runs it as its own user: that user must be able to read this directory and the folders below.
_test_by_hand: Make a request file (one name per line) and an SRIF file with the lines  Sysop x / AKA 1:110/100 / Baud 1 / Time -1 / RequestList /tmp/req.txt / ResponseList /tmp/rsp.txt / RemoteStatus PROTECTED  and run:  MKJSON=/etc/mkfreq mkfreq -S /tmp/srif.txt   then look at /tmp/rsp.txt (one +path line for each file found). The log lines say why a name was not found.

config._note: Our main address: used in the note a requester gets by netmail (only when the BBS tosser runs) and in the log.

files._note: Each folder that may be requested is a file area. Attr 32 = Allow file requests. FilePath is absolute, ends with a slash and is at most 50 characters (a longer one is cut short). A requester gets a file only from an area whose ViewSec and DLSec its request security meets (see Links and ReqSec below).

mailer._note: Flags 64 = answer file requests (mcFileReq). ReqSec is the file request security of a system that is not a link (or whose link has level 0): level 1 gets the areas of level 1 or less. ReqAttr: 1 = also answer sessions without a password, 2 = tell the requester by netmail (needs the MK tosser; leave it out here). ReqMaxFiles 0 = 20 files, ReqMaxKb 0 = no limit.

Links._note: A system you know gets its own request security instead of the one above: Level 0 = use ReqSec. Level 50 here also gets the Members only area.
